To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
omega-3 fatty-acid-rich diets suppress colon tumor growth in nude mice and this growth suppression is associated with a decrease in tumor cell proliferation and an increase in apoptosis.
dietary omega- 3 fatty acids suppress the growth of human colorectal cancer xenografts in athymic mice.

dietary omega- 3 fatty acids, particularly docosahexanoic acid, suppress the growth of human colonic carcinoma xenografts in nude mice and this growth inhibition is associated with changes in cytokine expression and apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of diet in colon cancer and the influence of dietary fat and fat components on the growth of colon cancer.
the effects of omega-3 and other fatty acids on colon cancer cell growth and the mechanisms of these effects.
the effects of omega-3 dietary fatty acids on human colon tumor growth in athymic mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary omega-6 fatty acid supplementation promotes tumor growth and that dietary omega- 3 fatty acid supplementation inhibits tumor growth.
omega-3 fatty acis are potent inhibitors of human colon carcinoma growth in vivo.
the omega-3 fatty-acids in fish oil are anti-carcinogenic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary supplementation of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) can inhibit colon carcinogenesis.
dietary supplementation with omega-3 fatty oils containing DHA (docosahexaenoeic acid) significantly inhibits colon tumor growth in athymic mice.
omega-3 fatty acyls are potent tumor suppressors in human colon carcinoma and that the omega-3 fatty alcohols are not as effective as the fatty acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary omega- 3 fatty acids have the potential to be used as a cancer chemoprevention agent for colon cancer.
the omega-3 fatty, docosahexenoic acid is a potent inhibitor of human colon cancer.
dietary omega- 3 fatty acids have a significant tumor growth inhibitory effect on the growth of colon carcinoma xenografted in athymic mice.
